hero.heroHeading: Building systems that hold up under real use.
hero.heroThesis: Backend-leaning software engineer with eight years building infrastructure, APIs, and the occasional interface, for teams that need things to keep working after launch day.

about.paragraph1: I spend most of my time in Go and TypeScript, working on services that sit close to data — queues, migrations, the parts of a system that are unglamorous until they break. Before that, I spent three years doing infrastructure work at a logistics company, which is where I learned to distrust anything that hasn't been tested under load.
about.paragraph2: Outside of client work, I maintain a couple of small open-source tools and write occasionally about database internals and the tradeoffs behind boring technology.

work.job1Desc: Lead engineer on the payments infrastructure team. Rebuilt the settlement pipeline to cut reconciliation errors by a wide margin, and introduced schema-versioning practices now used across four teams.
work.job2Desc: Built and operated the routing service handling live fleet data for a mid-size delivery network. Moved the team from nightly batch jobs to a streaming pipeline.
work.job3Desc: First engineering role, split between client web work and internal tooling for a small design studio.

projects.proj1Desc: An append-only ledger library for services that need auditable state changes without adopting a full event-sourcing framework.
projects.proj2Desc: A minimal job queue built for small teams who found existing options too heavy for their traffic. Around 400 stars on GitHub.
projects.proj3Desc: A command-line tool for logging and querying incident postmortems, built out of frustration with existing wiki-based systems.
